summary: A good deal of this neighbourhood was cemetery first. The Board took a deed from the Laurel Hill Cemetery Association for street purposes in 1926, and when Calvary Cemetery was given up it recorded that the abandonment "has opened a new area for sub-division"; Geary Boulevard was widened past the Anzavista tract in 1947, and in 1935 St. Rose's Avenue became Anza Street. The streets were then widened out of their own frontages — fourteen feet given up along Parker Avenue in 1927, eleven feet three inches taken off the west side of Presidio Avenue by 1947 — and the Board spent the interwar years fixing how far back a house had to stand, six feet then eight then ten along Parker Avenue. The same few corners kept coming back asking to move from the residential zone into the commercial one, Arguello at California, Bush at Presidio, California at Parker, and the Board and the Planning Commission disagreed about them for a decade. Under the houses went fuel oil, fifteen hundred gallons at a time. Since 2019 nearly the whole record has been a single block: 3333 California Street, on the old cemetery land, where the Board worked through a development agreement, a conditional use, a special use district, an encroachment permit across five streets, a map for 675 flats, and in 2025 a financing district to pay for the infrastructure. Smaller arguments run underneath: a foreign-language programme for children on Sacramento Street was appealed to the Board in 2008, and the environmental report for 3333 California was conditionally reversed in 2019. At 800 Presidio Avenue it made room for fifty affordable flats beside the Booker T. Washington Community Service Center. And it has written down three names: Theodore Roosevelt Middle School in 2019, the manzanita at 115 Parker Street in 2008, and Avery Street, renamed Boswell Way that same year for the Reverend Hamilton T. Boswell.
